title: Hiring, Onboarding, Roles, and Internal Tools — Company Handbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document describes Redwood's hiring and onboarding practices, role and career ladder expectations, a high-level summary of benefits and perks, and the internal tools and access process for new hires. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops, and new Redwood employees.

1) Hiring: process and roles

- Objective: hire for mission fit, technical skill, and operational maturity while moving candidates through a predictable and inclusive process.
- Interview stages (standard for IC engineering roles):
  1. Recruiter screen (30 minutes) — role fit, compensation expectations, logistics.
  2. Hiring manager hire-scope call (30-45 minutes) — team responsibilities and candidate questions.
  3. Technical screen (45-60 minutes) — coding/problem-solving or design fundamentals.
  4. Onsite / loop (3-4 interviews, 90-150 minutes) — system design, coding, culture & collaboration, role-specific exercise.
  5. Decision & offer — hiring manager + interview panel consensus; offers routed through people-ops.
- Diversity & inclusion: interview panels should include diverse perspectives when possible; use structured rubrics and calibrated scorecards.
- Typical timelines: target 3-6 weeks from first screen to offer for most roles.
- Hiring manager responsibilities: define role spec, interview rubrics, candidate feedback within 48 hours, and onboarding plan for first 90 days.

2) Offer and preboarding checklist

- Offer approvals: compensation band, manager sign-off, and people-ops compliance check.
- Preboarding tasks (people-ops):
  - Send offer letter and benefits summary.
  - Collect required I-9/ID documents (US) or local equivalents.
  - Start provisioning request to eng-ops for access and equipment ordering.
- New hire tasks: complete forms, select benefits, and pick start date.

3) Onboarding roadmap (first 90 days)

- Week 0 (before start): equipment delivery, redwoodctl login onboarding guide, and 30-minute manager sync scheduled.
- Week 1: orientation (company mission, org overview), HR paperwork, security training, and meet-the-team sessions.
- Weeks 2-4: role-specific training, shadowing, first small project, and expectations review at 30-day check-in.
- Days 30/60/90: formal check-ins with manager and people-ops; document progress, blockers, and career development goals.
- New hire mentor: assigned by manager; mentor meets weekly for first 8 weeks.

4) Roles and career ladders (summary)

- Levels and expectations (engineering example):
  - SDE I: junior contributor, learning systems and processes, delivers scoped tasks.
  - SDE II: independent contributor, owns features, participates in design.
  - Senior SDE: leads designs, mentors others, drives components.
  - Staff/Principal: cross-team technical leadership, sets architecture and standards.
- Promotion process: twice-yearly calibration cycles + exceptional promotions via manager case submission.
- Competency rubrics: engineering ladder includes technical impact, ownership, communication, and cross-team influence. Managers must maintain role profiles in Lattice/HRIS.

5) Benefits & perks (brief)

- Core benefits: competitive medical/dental/vision plans, 401(k) with match (US), parental leave policy, and flexible PTO.
- Perks: remote/hybrid work allowances, home office stipend, learning & development stipend, wellness reimbursement, commuter/parking benefits where applicable.
- Time off expectations: take time to recharge; managers approve PTO 2 weeks in advance when possible. See company-handbook-working-at-redwood for full benefits details.

6) Internal tools and access (engineering-focused)

- Access request flow (timeline: goal within 3 business days):
  1. People-ops creates initial HR record and equipment ticket.
  2. Manager files access provisioning request in Access Portal (link: https://access.redwood.internal) with required services listed.
  3. Infra/eng-ops and security review and grant access.
- Typical services and owners:
  | Service                         | Purpose                        | Owner Team         | Typical Access Level |
  |--------------------------------|--------------------------------|--------------------|----------------------|
  | GitHub                         | Source control                  | eng-developer-exp  | write (repo-scoped)  |
  | GCP/AWS account                | Cloud infra                     | eng-infra          | IAM role per team    |
  | Slack                          | Communication                   | eng-platform       | @new-hire onboarding |
  | Redwood Console (internal)     | Observability/ops               | eng-platform       | viewer -> dev        |
  | JIRA / Linear                  | Work tracking                   | eng-platform       | project access       |
  | Lattice / HRIS                 | Performance & HR                | people-ops         | employee record      |

- Onboarding CLI examples (run after email activation):
  # Install the CLI
  curl -fsSL https://downloads.redwood.internal/redwoodctl/install.sh | bash

  # Login and bootstrap workspace
  redwoodctl login --email you@company.com
  redwoodctl bootstrap --team my-team

- Security requirements: enable SSO, enroll device in device-management (MDM), and enable 2FA on all accounts before accessing production systems. Access to production requires manager approval and an approved runbook.

7) First project playbook (example for engineers)

- Goal: ship a small, end-to-end change in your first 30 days. Steps:
  1. Choose a small ticket with owner-approved scope.
  2. Pair with mentor to write a design doc (1-2 pages) in Confluence.
  3. Get PR reviewed by at least one senior on the team.
  4. Run integration tests and deploy to staging.
  5. Present a short demo at weekly team sync.

8) Escalations and support

- Blockers: raise to manager and mentor immediately. If access or equipment issues persist beyond 3 business days, escalate to people-ops@redwood.com.
- Incident reporting: report security incidents to secops@redwood.com and follow the incident-response runbook.

9) Appendix & links

- Rapid links:
  - Offer templates: /confluence/templates/offer-letters
  - Access Portal: https://access.redwood.internal
  - Equipment order form: /confluence/templates/equipment-order
  - Company handbook: /confluence/company-handbook/company-handbook-working-at-redwood-2026
  - Roles & ladders: /confluence/company-handbook/company-handbook-roles-and-onboarding-2026

If you are a hiring manager or new hire and have questions not covered here, contact people-ops@redwood.com or your assigned People Partner.
